Situating my practice: I work at the intersection of Information Technology expertise and robust design methodologies — combining user experience considerations with personal artistic expression.

Inspiration: My decision to pursue design was largely inspired by my sister, an alumna of the National Institute of Design (NID). I draw further inspiration from the supportive faculty and diverse student peers at Srishti, as well as the creative freedom inherent in design education.

Across my work, I move between research, visual thinking, prototyping and making. I'm especially interested in how different representational forms — symbolic and narrative — impact emotional connection, feelings of comfort, and the desire for personal space.

03 / Method

How I work through a question.

I don't assume the first visible problem tells the whole story. I work from what can be observed toward the patterns, structures and perspectives that may be shaping it.

01

Observe

Pay attention to people, context and what actually happens — including mind mapping and literature review.

02

Listen

Gather perspectives through contextual interviews, documenting thoughts, feelings and perspectives.

03

Connect

Cluster evidence through affinity mapping, identify themes and look for patterns across data points.

04

Reframe

Generate 100 ideas, refine through Crazy 8s — identify opportunities without assuming conclusions.

05

Test

Create probes and interactive experiences to make ideas tangible and learn from participant feedback.

05 / Project Interest

Designing a clearer service around a complex system.

For the Bosch Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) opportunity, I would be interested in understanding how auditors work with the existing technology, information and operational processes at the toll plaza — and where the service experience could be improved.

What I would investigate

  • Auditors' tasks and decision points across a working shift
  • Information they need and how it reaches them
  • How exceptions are reviewed, escalated and resolved
  • Handoffs between people, processes and technical systems
  • Psychological and emotional load of the auditor role

What I would aim to deliver

  • A current-state journey and service blueprint
  • Research-backed opportunities, prioritised by impact
  • A future-state workflow or service concept
  • A plan to test and measure improvements
  • Visual documentation accessible to the full project team

This is a proposed approach based on the project brief, not completed research at Mundka. The actual workflow and pain points would need to be established through fieldwork and discussion with the project team.
